No One Truly Dies in My Dungeon

Original ONGOING GameLit Portal Fantasy / Isekai Progression Strategy Multiple Lead Characters Action Adventure Drama Fantasy Reincarnation Male Lead Non-Human Lead Magic Dungeon Crawler Modern Knowledge Dungeon Core
3,289 Followers
828 Pages
483,173 Views

No one truly dies in Owen’s dungeon.

That doesn’t mean it’s safe.

After dying in an accident, Owen Ashford wakes as the core of a collapsing dungeon in another world—a world where dungeons are disasters waiting to happen, hungry labyrinths that lure adventurers in, kill them, and eventually spill monsters into the lands beyond their gates.

Owen knows exactly what he is supposed to become.

He chooses otherwise.

By repairing a broken trial-return system, Owen creates a dungeon where defeat does not have to be permanent. Adventurers can fall, bleed, and die within his halls, only to awaken outside—alive, shaken, scarred, and changed by the experience.

Every battle still hurts. Every mistake still matters. Every victory must be earned.

To survive, Owen must design a dungeon dangerous enough to sustain him, fair enough to teach, and rewarding enough to make adventurers come back.

A Dungeon Core progression fantasy about brutal trials, tactical adventuring, second chances, and a dungeon that refuses to become the monster it was meant to be.

New chapters Monday–Friday at 10:05 AM ET.

This story is originally written by me in Chinese and translated into English with AI assistance.

I personally review and revise every chapter to preserve the meaning, characterization, and intent of the original manuscript.

Discussion, casual conversation, differing opinions, and good-faith criticism are all welcome. I only ask that conversations engage with the story itself rather than focusing solely on hostility toward the use of AI.

Alric wakes up in another world with all the usual assumptions already in place: a sword, a system menu, and the quiet expectation that he’ll start acting like a hero.

He doesn’t.

Instead, he starts paying attention.

Coins circulate too long to make sense. Measurements are imprecise. Beer is sour, but everyone drinks it anyway. Magic exists, but no one can explain why it works when it does, because it usually works well enough.

As Alric tries to find his footing, he brings with him habits from a more systematic world: watching how things are done, tracking what’s missing, and assuming that inconsistencies point to underlying rules.

Sometimes they do.
Sometimes they reveal reasons things were never “fixed” in the first place.

This is a slow-burn isekai about logistics, brewing, and learning what happens when methodical thinking collides with a society that functions, imperfectly, on its own terms.

Progress is possible.
Improvement is not always welcome.

What to expect:
Slow burn observation with show rather than tell. 
A methodical, craft-focused fantasy about brewing, trade, and the consequences of practical innovation.
A blend between cozy slice-of-life and small business starting up in a new ecoscape.
This is a methodical progression story rather than a combat-focused one.
Less dungeon crawling. More ledgers, fermentation, and the occasional economic incident

Every mage in this world treats lightning as a blunt instrument. Asher treats it as a power supply.

Damian Tesla only wanted to live up to his family name, but died through electrocution by his own underfunded miniature railgun prototype. He wakes in the body of Asher, a five-year-old orphan in a world that runs on magic, and his new body can channel lightning like nothing on Earth. The impossible weapon finally has a power source: him.

But Vesperia is a small kingdom holding a single mountain pass against Ironhold, an empire that has already devoured four nations and wants a fifth. Lightning mages here don't get workshops. They get conscripted.

Whispers say the empire's war is only the beginning. Something older is stirring behind the storm that seals the north.

All Asher wants is to do his research in peace. But to get peace, he will need power. Armed with his knowledge of physics and a perfect lightning affinity, he only hopes it's enough for what's coming.

He died a nobody.
Now he’s reborn in a body beaten and left for dead, no family, no food, no future.

In the Kingdom of Avalon, strength isn’t just respected, it’s survival. Power is ranked by Tiers, magic is earned through blood and elemental affinity, and those without talent are nothing more than fodder for war.

Edward has neither noble blood nor rare talent. What he does have is an iron will, a sharp mind, and the stubborn refusal to stay down. Desperate for food, shelter, and a second chance, he enlists in the Royal Army, trading the uncertainty of the streets for the grueling discipline of military life.

But the army is no place for the weak. Training is brutal, resources are scarce, and every recruit is just one mistake away from the grave. Here, camaraderie is forged in hardship, tactics matter as much as raw strength, and survival demands more than swinging a sword, it demands learning, adapting, and enduring.

The road ahead is long and unforgiving. Yet with each step, Edward edges closer to something greater, growth, purpose, and perhaps a place in a kingdom that would rather see him buried than crowned.

Rise… or be forgotten.

What to expect:

  ~Slow-paced progression

  ~Non-OP

  ~Military focus

  ~Gritty, grounded tone

  ~No harem

They defy the heavens, but she defies the odds.

The young girl walks with a fluid grace across the blood-soaked fields of the Jinan plains.  Her emerald scholar’s robes and calm demeanor look completely out of place amongst the throngs of warring soldiers, still actively fighting and dying in the mud.  Unfazed by the violence all around her, she drifts across the battlefield like a jade phantom – a lost soul wandering amidst the hurricane of clashing steel.

But her travel is far from aimless.  And everywhere she steps, the impossible happens.

Spears intended for her heart find only empty air.  Gaps appear in previously impenetrable lines, as if from nowhere.  Orderly ranks of troops dissolve into calculated chaos.  And all the while, the heavy executioners of the Tai-shan sect follow in her wake, eager to reap their harvest of human lives.

The apparent miracle is a result of careful choreography, built upon a framework of troop formations, logistics, and probability.  Chae-ha controls it because she alone has realized the truth:

War is just math.  With consequences.

The Riftstorm dumps a new batch of accidental immigrants on planet Navar every year. This year, for the first time in two decades, one of them is human. And unlike his fellow arrivals, Eric Nevermore is a programmer.

Unfortunately, Navar has no convenient system for translations, levels, or power-ups. And instead of adventure and monster hunting, what awaits Eric is a magic school, years of language drills, ancient runes, and grinding study just to become a functional member of a society that doesn't even want him there.

So Eric has a better idea: learn magic the hard way, apply a few programming principles the Greys have never considered, and build his own system from scratch. 

All he needs is funding, some test subjects, and Sahirah – the pale, sharp-toothed Nadiri girl with more raw mana than she knows what to do with – to agree that the smartest thing they can do is drop out and start a company.

The only thing Eric fails to consider is that Navar's old money and established powers aren't keen on a soft-skinned off-worlder rewriting how magic works.

Once a legendary Archmage... Now a Level 1 Druid.

Aurelius spent centuries defying gods and mastering the arcane, reaching heights no mortal should touch.

Yet, as a half-elf, he was always an outcast; deemed "corrupted" and denied the very nature magic that was his birthright.

His reward for his brilliance? Betrayal and death.

As his life faded, a mysterious voice offered him a second chance. Reborn in a frail human body with zero mana, Aurelius is thrust into a world governed by the Astrae System: a cosmic meat-grinder that abducts humans from Earth and forces them through brutal trials.

To uncover the truth behind his betrayal and survive the trials, he must finally claim the power he was once forbidden to touch: the magic of nature and spirit.

Thea has always dreamt of joining the United Human Federation Marine Corps, ever since she was saved by one of their marines at a young age in the Undercity of Lumiosia.

Growing up in an undercity meant however, especially in a Mid-World such as Lumiosia, that she would have to work her way up from the very bottom. She would need to leave for one of the Inner- or Core-Worlds, before she had any chance of applying to the UHF Marines, but for that, she needed credits.

Having spent a lot of time in the local arcade for many years, she had accumulated a lot of technical knowledge in repairing the old-tech machines, as well as gained a high proficiency in a lot of the simulators and games featured.

Preparing for the monthly reset day, in which the ladders for each game get updated by the local quantum node and prizes are distributed for the top performers, she never would have anticipated a brand new challenge appearing from thin air.

A challenge which changed the path of her life forever...

Current release times: Tuesdays and Fridays at 8pm CEST / 2pm ET / 11am PT

Discord Link: https://discord.gg/rtZGz5RHtq

The Allbright System is an Epic Sci-Fi Progression LitRPG, heavily focused on war and the military complex as a whole. It is my first publicly published Webnovel, so I am very much looking forward to read all of your feedback and suggestions.

As the name suggests, there will be a System that governs the major progression and LitRPG elements of the story.

The main draw of this story will be the way that the System interacts with each Faction in the war for the galaxy, as each Faction gets a unique System-Trait for themselves. The nature of the Traits is to be a secret until further on in the story, but rest assured that they fundamentally change the way that war in this galaxy is waged.

Before you start reading this story, please be aware that this will not be a short one.

I prefer long, expansive stories that span thousands of pages, in order to fully tell the story I intend to tell.

The Prologue Arc itself, which culminates in the System integration, will be 21 Chapters long (around 300-350~ pages on RR), so if you are looking for a quick and short read, this story will not be for you.

For everyone else, I hope you will enjoy this length journey alongside me. I plan to give readers the option to choose on developments for the story or characters at later stages, where it makes sense, so please look forward to the reader polls at those times.

A major inspiration for this Webnovel is Duck_No_Duck's "Digital Marine", which unfortunately has been on a lengthy hiatus.

Further inspirations (more minor in scope, mostly regarding the litRPG and System elements) include, but aren't limited to, Azarinth Healer by Rhaegar and Beneath the Dragoneye Moons by Selkie.

Highly recommend you check them all out, if you're enjoying this story!

The protagonist of this story, an archaeologist specializing in dead languages, dies after finding a door that should not have existed and is reborn in another world, where, due to a very bad decision she does not remember making, she is denied any possibility of taking the most orthodox and fastest path of slaughter, so she has no choice but to take things slowly and follow the path of all those hidden masters, aided by her former talent for understanding and deciphering various languages.

What to expect:

-Strange as it may seem, this story is a Slice of Life cultivation novel, so things move slowly, don't expect a speed run of cultivation.

-Due to the protagonist's special circumstances, don't expect a lot of combat or fighting. And when there is, because it's still a cultivation world, it will always be brief and not too drawn out.

-The protagonist knows nothing about cultivation and isn't a regular reader of web novels, as is usually the case, so she starts from scratch and has to figure everything out little by little.

-The protagonist doesn't forget her old life or everything she knows about it in the first dozen episodes either, which—combined with the previous point—means she often compares what she discovers and learns in this new world with the things she knows from her old one.

-An attempt to make the characters interesting and with their own personalities. Only time will tell if I succeed or not.

-A unique and original cultivation system, don't expect Qi Realms and Golden Cores.
